title: £3.5m finance secured for Ringwood Corn Exchange scheme
summary:
Pallas Capital has provided £3.54 million in development finance to support the conversion of The Corn Exchange in Ringwood, a building that has remained vacant for more than 20 years. The 18-month facility will fund 12 residential units alongside ground-floor and basement commercial space.

The post £3.5m finance secured for Ringwood Corn Exchange scheme appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: St Albans development secures £12.5m finance package
summary:
Paragon Development Finance has provided a £12.5m facility to BQ Properties (St Albans) Limited for a mixed-use scheme at 67-69 St Peter's Street in St Albans city centre. The 22-month facility will fund construction of 34 residential units and three commercial units, with a projected gross development value of approximately £23.5m.

title: Letting agents face deposit compliance risk under new rules
summary:
Letting agents managing nearly 70% of England's protected tenancy deposits may face compliance issues following changes introduced under the Renters' Rights Act. The Letting Partnership warns that deposit registration processes linked to tenancy start dates rather than receipt of funds could result in breaches.

title: Birmingham letting agent reports 79% rise in new tenancies
summary:
A south Birmingham letting agent has reported a 79% increase in new rental properties during the first four months of 2026. Partridge Homes arranged 129 new lettings between January and April, contrasting with national data showing a 20% decline in UK rental demand.

title: New build property prices decline across five UK regions
summary:
New build property prices have fallen across five UK regions between April 2024 and April 2025, according to Propertymark data. Wales recorded the largest decline at approximately 5%, whilst five other regions saw price increases.

title: Letting agent successfully challenges council licensing scheme
summary:
A letting agency has successfully challenged Charnwood Borough Council's selective licensing conditions through the First-tier Tribunal, resulting in amendments affecting over 1,000 landlords. The case was settled through a Consent Order in March 2025 after AST Lettings Ltd argued that conditions exceeded statutory powers.

title: UK property tax burden highest among major economies
summary:
The United Kingdom has the highest property tax burden among major economies at 3.7% of GDP, according to analysis by property tax specialist Ryan. Britain collected just over £100 billion last year through council tax, business rates, stamp duty and land taxes.

The post UK property tax burden highest among major economies appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Reform UK proposes repeal of Renters’ Rights Act
summary:
Reform UK has announced plans to repeal the Renters' Rights Act through a proposed 'Great Repeal Bill' if the party wins the next General Election. Industry professionals have responded with caution, suggesting that reversing the legislation would require more comprehensive solutions than a simple repeal.

title: Stamp duty changes could add 168,000 property sales
summary:
Research suggests that reforming stamp duty charges for property traders could increase UK housing transactions by up to 178% annually. The study found that removing the Higher Rate for Additional Dwellings surcharge for corporate traders could generate an additional 168,000 property sales each year.

title: Up Estates opens third Rugby branch with fixed fee model
summary:
Independent estate agency Up Estates has opened a third office in Rugby, expanding its presence in the Warwickshire town as part of its regional growth strategy. The new branch on Regent Street will offer residential sales and lettings services using the company's fixed fee pricing model.
